discussion_comments.comment_body:
Fixed - `setModelCatalogOnContext` now clears the key instead of skipping when no catalog is configured:

```go
catalog := bifrost.getModelCatalog()
if catalog == nil {
    ctx.ClearValue(schemas.BifrostContextKeyModelCatalog)
    return
}
ctx.SetValue(schemas.BifrostContextKeyModelCatalog, catalog)
```

The reachable path is the reused-context one: `RunPreHooks` (core/bifrost.go) re-enters this per WS message on a long-lived context, so a context stamped before a `SetModelCatalog(nil)` would have kept serving the retired catalog to every later hook. That also contradicted `SetModelCatalog`'s own doc ("Safe to call at any time; nil clears it").

Two clarifications on the finding: `BifrostContextKeyModelCatalog` is not in `reservedKeys` (core/schemas/context.go:14), so there is no restricted-writes gate on either call. And `ClearValue` is a no-op when the context has no values map, so SDK users who never wire a catalog still pay nothing - the doc comment was updated to say so rather than claiming the whole function no-ops.

Read-back stays safe: `GetModelInfo`/`CalculateCost` use the comma-ok assertion, so the cleared nil yields `catalog == nil` and returns nil/0.

discussion_comments.comment_body:
Fixed — resolved in the other direction you offered ("drop the earlier nil checks").

`listModelsReq` cannot be nil here: `ListModelsRequest` rejects a nil request at `core/bifrost.go:656` and is the only constructor of this request type (the sole `RequestType = schemas.ListModelsRequest` assignment on a request object is at line 686, immediately followed by `bifrostReq.ListModelsRequest = req`). Every other match is `ExtraFields.RequestType` on a response or error.

So the two guards were redundant rather than the dereferences being unsafe. Extending them instead would have added three unreachable branches and still left the pre-existing unguarded dereference in the cached branch, so it would not have reached the consistency you flagged. Both guards are gone and a comment now records the invariant. See updated code.

// Reasoning
 	// gpt-oss models include only reasoning_text content blocks in a message, while other openai models include summaries+encrypted_content
 	*ResponsesReasoning
+
+	// rawToolSearch preserves codex `tool_search_call` / `tool_search_output`
+	// items verbatim. OpenAI's Responses API accepts these natively, but
+	// Bifrost's typed schema doesn't model them (the call's `arguments` is a
+	// JSON object — unlike function_call's string — and the output carries a
+	// `tools` array). Rather than fail to deserialize the whole input array or
+	// drop/mangle these items, we round-trip the original bytes unchanged.
+	// Set by UnmarshalJSON, emitted by MarshalJSON; nil for every other type.
+	rawToolSearch []byte
+}
+
+// isToolSearchItem reports whether t is a codex tool_search item type, which
+// Bifrost preserves verbatim rather than modelling field-by-field.
+func isToolSearchItem(t string) bool {
+	return t == string(ResponsesMessageTypeToolSearchCall) ||
+		t == string(ResponsesMessageTypeToolSearchOutput)
+}
+
+// UnmarshalJSON preserves codex tool_search items verbatim (see rawToolSearch)
+// and defers every other item type to the default struct decoding.
+func (m *ResponsesMessage) UnmarshalJSON(data []byte) error {
+	if t := gjson.GetBytes(data, "type").String(); isToolSearchItem(t) {
+		mt := ResponsesMessageType(t)
+		*m = ResponsesMessage{Type: &mt, rawToolSearch: append([]byte(nil), data...)}
+		return nil
+	}
+	type alias ResponsesMessage
+	return sonic.Unmarshal(data, (*alias)(m))

discussion_comments.comment_body: Good catch — addressed in `feb24bba7`. `ResponsesMessage.UnmarshalJSON` now resets the receiver (`*m = ResponsesMessage{}`) before either branch, so a reused instance can't retain stale `rawToolSearch`. Not reachable via the array-decode path (each element starts zero), but applied as a defensive correctness fix. Round-trip + schemas tests pass.

By design. `UpdateProvider` modifies the request's own provider field (e.g. `BifrostChatRequest.Provider`) directly. `getProviderQueue` reads the provider from `preReq.GetRequestFields()`, which already reflects the plugin's change. A separate `ProviderOverride.Provider` field would be a second source of truth for the same value — creating inconsistency risk if one is set without the other.
